overview: Systems keep moving onshore from the Pacific, favoring the Cascades and Coast Mountains through Thanksgiving, then a drier stretch. The northern Rockies get a band of snow Friday into Saturday. The Northeast gets a storm this week, then more snow later.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: A wet, mild pattern takes over here. Rain falls with snow at times through Thursday, and snow levels sit high. The top resort, Whistler, has 34 inches on the books, but most of it came in the first two days, and the rest of the week leans toward rain. Expect slush at lower elevations and better conditions higher up.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A series of fronts keeps the Cascades unsettled through Thursday. Snow levels stay above the passes, so the mountains get rain and wet snow at the lower elevations. Mt. Baker is the top resort, with a 17 inch total, and a Winter Storm Watch starts Thursday. Expect wind as the systems pass. The weekend brings a brief lull before the next active spell.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: The week starts dry and mild in Wyoming and Montana, with morning fog in the valleys. A system arrives Friday and brings snow to western Wyoming through Saturday, with a chance of snow east of the Divide Saturday. Jackson Hole has a 9 inch total, and the NWS is calling for more, 12 to 25 inches Thursday night through Sunday night. Grand Targhee sees a similar pattern, with the NWS forecasting 20 to 34 inches.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Rain and mountain snow move through Tahoe overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, with snow levels around 6,000 to 7,000 feet. Wind picks up behind the front. Dry, seasonable weather follows through Thanksgiving and into the early weekend, with valley fog. The next chance of snow comes Sunday, when Kirkwood, Sugar Bowl and Palisades are all forecast about 7 inches.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A Thanksgiving storm brings wintry precipitation to the Great Lakes and interior Northeast, and the coast deals with strong winds and flooding. Le Massif gets snow and rain Friday, then a mix of flurries and showers through the weekend. Mont-Sainte-Anne sees rain mixing with snow. A Special Weather Statement runs from Friday to Saturday. Blue Mountain in Ontario sees 4 inches Thursday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
